name: Alay Valley
near: For different parts of the valley — Sary-Tash (~3200 m, the fork of the Pamir Highway), Sary-Mogol (~2980 m, the base for Lenin Peak and Tulpar-Kul), Daroot-Korgon in the west (I Love KG). The catalog point lies between Sary-Mogol and Kashka-Suu.
elev: On average about 3000 m (too.kg); Sary-Tash ~3200 m, Sary-Mogol ~2980 m, Tulpar-Kul ~3500 m, Taldyk Pass at the entrance — 3615 m (I Love KG).
short: The Alay Valley is a wide high-mountain (~3000 m) intermontane basin between the Alay and Trans-Alay ranges with a view of Lenin Peak (7134 m); the Pamir Highway runs through it.
desc: The Alay Valley is an intermontane basin in southern Kyrgyzstan between the Alay and Trans-Alay ranges, about 120 km in a straight line from Osh (too.kg); the average elevation is about 3000 m, and the width ranges from 8–10 to 25 km (too.kg). The relief was leveled by ancient glaciation. Above the valley stands the wall of the Trans-Alay Range with Lenin Peak (7134 m), whose base camp is reached by roads from the valley (too.kg). The Pamir Highway Osh — Khorog runs through the valley, popular with cyclists and motorcyclists, and in ancient times a branch of the Great Silk Road ran here (too.kg). The valley remains a center of nomadic herding: in summer the slopes are dotted with yurts and camps (too.kg). The main villages are Sary-Tash, Sary-Mogol and Daroot-Korgon (I Love KG).
guide: The best way to meet the Alay is from Taldyk Pass (3615 m): after the last bend the whole valley opens up, with the wall of the Trans-Alay and Lenin Peak. Base yourself in Sary-Mogol — from here it is 25 km to Lake Tulpar-Kul and the yurt camps at the foot of Lenin. Don't rush: Sary-Tash and Sary-Mogol sit at 3000–3200 m, and a headache on the first evening is a signal to stop, not to climb higher (I Love KG). A border permit is not needed for the highway and Sary-Mogol, but it is needed for Achyk-Tash and the base camp (I Love KG). If you catch the third weekend of July, Sary-Mogol hosts a festival of horse and yak games (Visit Alay).
see: The panorama of the Trans-Alay Range and Lenin Peak (7134 m); Taldyk Pass (3615 m); Lake Tulpar-Kul and the Achyk-Tash base camp; yurts and nomads' herds; the Pamir Highway (too.kg, I Love KG).
skip: You tolerate altitude poorly and cannot set aside a day for acclimatization (I Love KG). You are going in the off-season — the yurt camps close in September, and in spring there is snow on Taldyk (I Love KG). You have one day from Osh — that is 4+ hours each way.
diff: Driving through the valley is easy (the paved highway); the main difficulty is the altitude of 3000–3600 m (I Love KG). Treks from Sary-Mogol and Tulpar-Kul: Travellers' Pass ~4100 m (5 h round trip — Visit Alay), the multi-day “Best of Alay” 123 km with passes up to 4306 m (Visit Alay).
when: June — August (I Love KG); the yurt camps operate in summer and close in September; in spring there may be snow on Taldyk, in summer thunderstorms, and the nights are cold (I Love KG). Trekking — June to early September (Visit Alay).
hours: Open territory; the Osh — Sary-Tash road is open year-round (in winter Taldyk may be closed because of snow — editorial). Achyk-Tash and the Lenin Peak base camp — with a border permit (I Love KG).
daytime: Morning — clear visibility of Lenin Peak and the Trans-Alay; by evening clouds and thunderstorms (I Love KG, TripAdvisor on Tulpar-Kul).
how: From Osh along the Pamir Highway via Gulcha and Taldyk Pass (3615 m) to Sary-Tash, then west to Sary-Mogol (~220 km, ~4 h of pure driving — I Love KG) or to Daroot-Korgon. Marshrutka (minibus) Osh → Sary-Mogol — one trip at 14:00 (schedule for 27.08.2026 — I Love KG), arriving ~18:00, 300 som (Backpack Adventures).
needcar: Yes: marshrutka/shared taxi to the villages of the valley, then local cars to the lakes and camps (transfer to Tulpar-Kul ~1 h — I Love KG).
self: Yes: marshrutka/taxi to Sary-Mogol or Sary-Tash, accommodation in guesthouses, a transfer to the lake on the spot; no permit is needed for the highway and Sary-Mogol, but it is needed for Achyk-Tash/the base camp (I Love KG).
roadtype: The main approach from Osh via Taldyk is the paved Pamir Highway (too.kg); turn-offs to pastures, Tulpar-Kul and the camps are dirt roads (Visit Alay; editorial).
traveltime: Osh → Sary-Mogol: ~220 km, ~4 h of pure driving, longer with stops (I Love KG); marshrutka 14:00 → ~18:00 (Backpack Adventures); Sary-Mogol → Tulpar-Kul ~45 min–1 h.
stay: Guesthouses in Sary-Mogol with meals — $15–20 with breakfast (Backpack Adventures; year not stated); yurt camps at Tulpar-Kul in summer — from 1000 som/night with breakfast and dinner (Visit Alay); CBT Sary-Mogol (sarymogol.com, +996 556 092627) books accommodation.
net: Not confirmed by operator: in Sary-Mogol the Wi-Fi is unreliable and a local SIM is recommended (Backpack Adventures); I Love KG advises an offline map and a power bank.
entry: There is no entrance fee for the valley. A border permit costs ≈$35–40 (Visit Alay FAQ, 07.2026), takes 1–2 weeks, and is needed for the Lenin Peak base camp (I Love KG, Visit Alay); it is not needed for the highway and Sary-Mogol (I Love KG).
transfer: Osh → Sary-Mogol: marshrutka 300 som, shared taxi 400 som/seat, private car ~3000 som (Backpack Adventures); Sary-Mogol → Tulpar-Kul 1500 som/car (Visit Alay). The year of the Backpack Adventures data is not stated — check for 2026.
bring: Cash, an offline map, warm clothes, sun protection, a power bank, a flashlight (I Love KG); passport and permit if you are going to Achyk-Tash.
warn: Altitude 3000–3600 m: a headache and nausea are a reason to stop and not climb higher (I Love KG). Snow on Taldyk in spring, thunderstorms in summer, cold nights (I Love KG). The border zone at Achyk-Tash/the base camp and along the border with Tajikistan — a permit is needed.
food: Home-style Kyrgyz cooking in the guesthouses of Sary-Mogol and in yurts (dinner and breakfast are included in the 1000 som — Visit Alay); kymyz and ayran from nomads in summer (too.kg: nomadic herding; editorial).
reviews: Google Maps “Alay Valley”: 4.5/5, 8 ratings (03.10.2026). For related places: TripAdvisor Tulpar-Kol 4.7/5 (9 reviews, until 07.2025). Pluses: views of Lenin Peak, nomadic culture, treks; minuses: altitude, changeable weather, the long road. TripAdvisor “Base Camp For Peak Lenin” (in the valley): 4.7/5, 58 reviews, No. 2 of 23 in Osh; 2025 reviews: yurt camps from basic to “hotel-like”.
p.sum: The Alay Valley is a high-mountain (about 3000 m) steppe between the Alay and Trans-Alay ranges; the gateways are Sary-Tash (the fork of the Pamir Highway) and Sary-Mogol (the base for Tulpar-Kul and Lenin Peak). From Osh it is 4–5 h on paved road via Taldyk: the 14:00 marshrutka from the New Bus Station (300 som) or a shared taxi 400–500 som/seat, a private car ~3000–4500 som. For overnight stays — guesthouses in Sary-Tash and Sary-Mogol ($10–20) and yurt camps on the jailoo (summer pasture) in summer; there are no ATMs — withdraw cash in Osh. A permit is needed only for Achyk-Tash and the border area.

p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Tulpar-Kul and the Achyk-Tash base camp; Kojokelen and the Kosh-Kol lakes; the Pamir Highway to Murghab via Kyzyl-Art (GBAO permit); on the way back — Kichi-Alay/Abshir-Ata via Nookat.
p.season: June–August is the best time (camps are working, dry, afternoon thunderstorms); July — the festival of horse and yak games; September — camps close, frosty nights; October–May — snow, Taldyk Pass is cleared but closures are possible; in winter ski touring near Taldyk.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka 300 som ×2 + guesthouse $15 + food ~600 som/day → ~3000–4000 som/person for 2–3 days
p.budget.comfort: Private car 3000–4500 som per car one way + guesthouses/Ak-Sai yurts $65–85, or a Visit Alay tour $850/8 days
p.permits: No permit is needed for the highway, Sary-Tash and Sary-Mogol (I Love KG 2026). For Achyk-Tash / the Lenin Peak base camp and the border area with Tajikistan — a border permit (Visit Alay ~$35–40, 1–2 weeks; on your own via tour.too.kg 3000 som, 5–7 working days). To enter Tajikistan via Kyzyl-Art — a visa/e-visa and a GBAO permit.
p.access: With children and older people — a trip along the highway and a night in a guesthouse are realistic, but the altitude of 3000+ m requires acclimatization; with a wheelchair — only on paved road / in a car; with a dog — possible, but be careful of shepherd dogs on the jailoo.
